changes.why: CR-025-01. GIT_ERRORS gains UnicodeDecodeError, with the comment moved above the constant to say why: _stdout and is_repo decode git strictly (text=True, encoding='utf-8'), so a non-UTF-8 commit subject or branch name raises an error that is neither an OSError nor a SubprocessError and escaped the per-project boundary, failing every pass and writing nothing for as long as the condition lasted. No collision with the load_data carve-out, which is outside the confined block and raises a plain ValueError. This is the only line of production code this round changes; tabs.carry is left exactly as it was, per the reviewer's adjudication.

CR-025-01's failing test, written and confirmed red before the fix. FakeRun gains raw: bytes for a repository or one of its commands, decoded with the encoding the caller asked for exactly as subprocess.run decodes under text=True, so the UnicodeDecodeError is git's own output and not a hand-made exception. PerProjectFailures.test_non_utf8_git_output_is_confined drives b'...Caf\xe9 fix' out of alpha's git log call through the command line and asserts the failure is confined. No existing case changed.

CR-025-02. The statuses half of the Case tearDown, deleted in round 1, is restored as an assertion of the rows a pass should have written: the stored status ids equal the statusDoc paths of every project any pass in the scenario was configured with (the empty set for the many scenarios that configure none). That keeps the every-scenario invariant the original guard existed for -- no status record the pass should not write -- and is true of the new behaviour, including the scenario where a project leaves the config and its project record is deleted while its status record is deliberately kept. One test that drives run_pass directly declares its config to the guard through Env.seen.

CR-025-02's plumbing, and the smallest way to make the restored guard exact rather than a weaker subset check. Env records, per pass, the statusDoc of every project the config names, read through exporters/board_config.projects -- the same loader the pass uses, so the default 'status/<id>' form and the validation rules are not restated in the tests. A config that loader refuses names no project a pass could write a status for, and the pass refuses it too, so it contributes nothing.

Unchanged this round. The git tab's pure half moved into the shared module: git_default (the master/main/'' selection) and git_doc (the whole document from captured stdout, applying the ahead/shortstat emptiness rule itself), plus public_remote and its USERINFO pattern. No subprocess, no file read.

Unchanged this round. git_tab is a thin caller of derive.git_default and derive.git_doc, keeping its ten subprocess calls and their order; public_remote and USERINFO are re-exported through the existing import line. Output unchanged.

follow_ups.ref: errors='replace' for the git subprocesses -- spec question, not taken
follow_ups.reason: The reviewer noted decoding git with errors='replace' would also close CR-025-01 but would diverge from export_board's decoding, so it belongs in the spec rather than in a code change. The module is at the marketplace path and defines validate(obj) -> [errors], but it has no __main__ block, so 'python change_report_schema.py <path>' runs nothing and exits 0 whatever the file says. Any round that needs a real check must import it and call validate().
